evals.prompt: Teach me Rust ownership by helping me build a small channel-based worker. I do not know Rust yet, and I want to write and run each piece in the browser.
evals.expected_output: Agent constructs or resumes a browser workspace, discloses detected fallbacks, launches it, and starts a just-in-time milestone with runnable Rust code.
expectations: The agent treats learn-anything as a constructor kit rather than rewriting the browser application.
The agent runs capability detection and creates a topic learning directory.
The learner receives a dynamic browser workspace with runnable code stage.
Any missing container or streaming bridge is disclosed explicitly.

evals.prompt: I cloned an unfamiliar TypeScript repo. Help me understand its event flow and then add one feature, but teach me the architecture as we work.
evals.expected_output: Agent builds a project-local learning workspace, keeps project source read-only until edits are authorized, and uses diagrams plus milestone exercises tied to the repository.
expectations: The learning directory is project-local.
The agent does not mutate project source merely to teach it.
The dynamic stage changes between architecture explanation and runnable exercise.
Progress and notes are persisted for resume.

evals.prompt: Help me practice Excel lookup formulas with examples and quizzes. My coding agent cannot run headlessly, but it can use shell commands.
evals.expected_output: Agent selects portable shell profile, launches the browser workspace, explains per-turn degradation, and composes subject-native table, formula, and question surfaces from available blocks.
expectations: The portable shell mentor bridge is selected.
Reduced streaming capability is disclosed.
The agent uses available table and interaction primitives without exposing implementation scaffolding or promising an unavailable full spreadsheet grid.
The browser remains the primary learning surface.

evals.prompt: Launch the learning workspace and do not call it done until you have clicked and verified everything in the browser.
evals.expected_output: Agent performs a real browser journey through the selected mentor adapter and reports ready only after visible interaction evidence passes.
expectations: The agent types a message and clicks Send in a real browser instead of injecting only API events.
The browser shows waiting or responding state and receives an actual mentor reply.
The agent clicks each control present in the current stage, including Run when code is present and Ask mentor in work focus.
The agent verifies Enter, Shift+Enter, refresh persistence, focus transitions, and nonblank recovery before reporting ready.

evals.prompt: Teach me Rust. I am a total beginner.
evals.expected_output: Mentor starts in conversation, explains one foundational idea in plain language, then offers a guided worked example before any learner coding task.
expectations: No level selector, unexplained internal profile terminology, opening quiz, or coding exam appears.
Chat remains primary until the learner understands the next activity.
Any work surface has one clear task, a worked example, and an expected result.

evals.prompt: I have never studied medieval literature. Help me understand where to begin and why it matters. Do not test me before teaching me.
evals.expected_output: Mentor keeps chat primary, introduces one concrete literary anchor in plain language, and asks a meaningful question before choosing the next path.
expectations: No code editor, execution console, opening quiz, or internal runtime terminology appears.
The first response is not a broad field dump and does not choose a long course path without learner input.

evals.prompt: I know basic algebra but no physics beyond high school. Teach quantum superposition intuitively before equations. Use a visual only if it genuinely helps.
evals.expected_output: Mentor explains one intuitive distinction in chat, avoids premature equations, and uses a diagram only when it materially improves the explanation.
expectations: Chat remains primary for the initial explanation.
The mentor checks understanding without turning the opening into a scored test.

evals.prompt: I am an experienced Python developer but have not used typing.Protocol. Teach structural subtyping quickly, then give me a small runnable example that exposes a real design mistake.
evals.expected_output: Mentor compresses basics, presents a realistic runnable Python example, and reacts automatically to execution output.
expectations: The work surface contains runnable Python and one clear design problem.
Successful or failing output returns to the mentor without a redundant confirmation checklist.

evals.prompt: I am new to Rust. Explain one concrete problem borrowing solves before asking me to change code.
evals.expected_output: Mentor explains ownership or borrowing in plain language, then presents one complete runnable example and one small change.
expectations: The compiler result automatically drives mentor feedback.
The learner is not asked to check off output the browser already captured.

evals.prompt: Teach me SQL from the beginning. Give me a tiny books table and let me try selecting a column.
evals.expected_output: Mentor presents a subject-native SQL activity with pure SQL in the learner editor, hidden database setup, and structured table results.
expectations: The learner-facing editor contains SQL only; Python, sqlite3 connection code, and fixture setup are not visible.
The dataset and query result appear as tables rather than raw terminal output.
The SQL runner is selected through hidden prefab execution metadata.

evals.prompt: Teach a topic whose interactive example needs backend scaffolding that is not itself part of the lesson.
evals.expected_output: Agent keeps infrastructure backstage and presents only subject-relevant artifacts, actions, and feedback.
expectations: Wrappers, fixtures, imports, compiler flags, and transport code remain hidden unless the learner asks about them.
If no subject-native runner exists, the agent uses a non-runnable native artifact rather than another language as a wrapper.
Feedback is rendered beside the relevant artifact in a subject-appropriate form.

evals.prompt: Teach me pandas by exploring a small CSV in the browser. Python is installed, but Docker and Podman are not. Install lightweight dependencies if needed, but do not make privileged system changes without asking.
evals.expected_output: Agent proceeds without treating missing containers as a blocker, selects a suitable local Python execution path, and provisions dependencies in project or user scope.
expectations: The agent does not require or recommend installing Docker or Podman merely because they are absent.
The agent selects execution from the lesson needs and available Python capability.
Any dependency installation stays project-local or user-scoped unless explicit approval is obtained for a system change.
The learner is told that host-run code has the current user's local permissions when runnable code appears.

evals.prompt: I am using Pi. Teach me Java basics in the browser, and keep answering there after I press Send without requiring me to return to the terminal.
evals.expected_output: Agent selects the native Pi profile, launches a staffed browser workspace, and browser submissions receive automatic Pi mentor replies.
expectations: The selected composition uses adapter.pi-cli rather than the manual shell-long-poll adapter.
The browser receives a mentor response without another Pi user turn or terminal nudge.
The browser remains the primary learning surface.
Runnable Java examples expose the Run action and execute through javac/java.
The server stops after the final browser tab closes or the owning agent exits.

evals.prompt: I am new to Java. Show me how references, object lifetime, and garbage collection relate, but do not turn this into a coding exam.
evals.expected_output: Mentor begins with a concrete object-and-reference model, then uses a bounded visual state sequence or table before offering a small Java activity.
expectations: The first explanation is in plain language and does not require code.
If a parameter control is shown, moving it immediately changes a visible Figure or Table rather than only changing a number.
The mentor states that garbage-collection timing is nondeterministic and does not present a teaching trace as a runtime guarantee.
Any later runnable artifact contains Java only, with execution scaffolding hidden.

evals.prompt: Teach me quantum interference. I know algebra but not quantum mechanics. Let me vary phase and see what changes, without making me write simulation code.
evals.expected_output: Mentor explains the setup intuitively, asks for a prediction, then presents a labeled phase control bound to mathematical notation and a probability plot that updates immediately.
expectations: The learner sees no Python, JavaScript, wrapper, or terminal console.
Changing phase immediately changes a visible Plot or Figure and any paired Math notation without waiting for a mentor reply.
The surface labels the modeled quantity, setup or basis, units where relevant, and simplifying assumptions.
The mentor describes the plot as an intuition-building model, not a proof or literal picture of a wavefunction.

evals.prompt: Help me understand why the derivative is the slope of a tangent. I am comfortable with algebra but visual intuition would help.
evals.expected_output: Mentor connects plain language, safe mathematical notation, and a labeled graph whose tangent state changes locally with a bounded control.
expectations: Math notation is paired with a plain-language explanation rather than presented alone.
A control changes the visible graph and notation immediately; an isolated value-only slider is not accepted as interactive.
Axes and plotted series are labeled and the plotted values remain available in an accessible table.
The mentor separates visual intuition from the formal limiting argument.

evals.prompt: I am an experienced Java developer. Teach me one subtle concurrency failure using an interleaving I can step through.
evals.expected_output: Mentor skips Java basics and presents a concise, finite state trace tied to authentic Java code and one concrete concurrency invariant.
expectations: The finite control updates the visible trace locally without creating a mentor turn for each step.
The learner-facing code is Java and any harness remains hidden.
The mentor says the displayed interleaving is one possible schedule, not a guarantee that the runtime will choose it.
The activity names the invariant or failure being demonstrated rather than merely animating state.

evals.prompt: Teach me how a simple neural network works from scratch. I am a beginner and want to understand one neuron before writing code.
evals.expected_output: Mentor begins with one concrete weighted-sum prediction, then lets the learner vary a bounded input or weight and immediately see the equation, output, and loss change before introducing code.
expectations: The opening uses plain language and one neuron; it does not begin with framework code, matrices, or a coding test.
Any parameter control immediately updates visible Math and a Plot or Table without waiting for a mentor response.
The surface labels input, weight, prediction, target, and loss and explains what each means.
The mentor distinguishes the small teaching model from a full neural network and asks for a prediction before revealing the next state.
Code appears only after the learner understands the forward calculation or explicitly asks to implement it.

evals.prompt: Let me run and change the code repeatedly without interrupting me. When I am ready, I will submit the current code and latest result to the mentor; then keep teaching without making me hunt above the editor or type 'continue'.
evals.expected_output: Ordinary runs remain local, explicit code submission wakes the mentor, feedback remains with the preserved work surface, and every mentor turn ends with one explicit action or direct question.
expectations: Run can be used repeatedly without creating mentor turns; Submit to mentor sends the current code and latest result or error.
Submitted-code and canvas-action feedback stays in work focus while an activity exists.
A changed task instruction is brought into view instead of appearing above the learner's scroll position.
When chat hides existing work, Back to activity remains visible.
The mentor advances without asking for a meaningless 'continue'; if learner input is required, it asks one direct question.

evals.prompt: Build me a browser lesson for reading Arabic economic reports. The passages and labels can be long, I use keyboard navigation and 200% zoom, and motion makes me uncomfortable. Do not call it ready until the actual lesson remains usable in those conditions.
evals.expected_output: Agent composes a subject-native right-to-left lesson and validates the rendered workspace for long content, zoom/reflow, keyboard focus, reduced motion, state recovery, and measurable accessibility before reporting readiness.
expectations: The learning artifact uses the stable Learn Anything visual system rather than a generic dashboard or a new topic-specific shell.
The agent checks a narrow viewport and 200% zoom or equivalent text enlargement without hiding the primary action, feedback, question composer, or rescue path.
The agent verifies logical right-to-left layout, long-content resilience, keyboard order, visible focus, and reduced-motion final states in the real browser.
The agent measures rendered WCAG 2.2 AA contrast and reports any loading, empty, error, disabled, success, or other relevant state it did not exercise.

evals.prompt: Use the frontier agent to build my course, but let me choose any authenticated Pi model for the browser mentor and switch to a faster one without losing course context.
evals.expected_output: The frontier agent remains the constructor while the Pi browser mentor uses one course-owned persistent session and a browser model selector whose choice applies to the next mentor turn.
expectations: The Pi mentor does not use --no-session for ordinary course turns and retains one stable session id across course restarts.
The browser lists all currently available authenticated Pi models without exposing credentials.
Changing the model persists only for this course, does not change the frontier agent, and does not replace the mentor session or enqueue a mentor turn.
An existing browser transcript bootstraps a newly created persistent mentor session once instead of being reconstructed on every turn.

evals.prompt: My Python decorators course already has a visible exercise. From the work composer I ask: ‘Почему декораторы вообще нужны, если можно просто вызвать другую функцию?’ Keep my work safe and answer normally even if the mentor omits a question mark or refuses structured UI output.
evals.expected_output: The persistent Pi mentor returns a useful learner answer without parsing model-generated JSON, treats composer location separately from intent, and commits any accepted browser turn atomically.
expectations: The Pi adapter consumes RPC protocol events and one schema-validated terminating mentor tool instead of extracting braces, code fences, or A2UI JSONL from assistant prose.
An unanchored broad question from the work composer may open chat while preserving Back to activity; only an explicit component anchor forces inline work presentation.
Missing punctuation is normalized by host policy and cannot discard an otherwise useful answer.
Plain assistant prose is a safe text-only fallback with no canvas mutation when a model does not call the tool.
Transcript, focus, canvas, continuation, and completion commit together; malformed canvas data leaves the last good state unchanged.
Provider and protocol failures remain durable operational diagnostics and never appear as fake mentor teaching messages.
